q.t: In a bar graph, all the bars must have the same:
q.e: Only the height should carry the information. If widths differed, a fat bar would look bigger than it really is.

q.t: In a bar graph, the value of each item is shown by the bar’s:
q.e: A taller bar means a bigger number — that is how you compare at a glance.

q.t: The scale is 1 unit = 5 students. A bar is 6 units high. How many students does it show?
The gaps between the bars of a bar graph should be:
o: Zero for the first two bars
q.e: Equal spacing keeps the picture fair and easy to read.

q.t: Books sold: Mon 20, Tue 35, Wed 25, Thu 40. Which day has the tallest bar?
q.e: The tallest bar belongs to the largest value, 40.

q.t: Books sold: Mon 20, Tue 35, Wed 25, Thu 40. How many books were sold in all?
q.e: Add the heights of all the bars: 20 + 35 + 25 + 40 = 120.

q.t: Books sold: Mon 20, Tue 35, Wed 25, Thu 40. How many more were sold on Thursday than on Monday?
The scale is 1 cm = 10 students. How long is the bar for 70 students (in cm)?
In a vertical bar graph, the horizontal axis usually shows:
q.e: Items (days, sports, classes) go along the bottom; the numbers go up the side.

q.t: A double bar graph is used to:
o: Compare two sets of data side by side
Show one set of data twice
q.e: Two bars for each item — for example boys and girls — let you compare within and across items.

q.t: 100 students chose a favourite sport: Cricket 45, Football 30, Hockey 15, Tennis 10. What fraction chose football?
100 students chose a favourite sport: Cricket 45, Football 30, Hockey 15, Tennis 10. What percent chose cricket?
Favourite sport: Cricket 45, Football 30, Hockey 15, Tennis 10. Find the ratio of hockey to cricket.
The scale is 1 unit = 4 km. A bar is 7.5 units long. What distance does it show (in km)?
Favourite sport: Cricket 45, Football 30, Hockey 15, Tennis 10. How many more chose cricket than hockey and tennis together?
The scale is 1 cm = 25. How long is the bar for 175 (in cm)?
The largest value in a data set is 500 and the axis can be 10 cm long. Which scale fits best?
q.e: 500 ÷ 10 cm = 50 per cm, so the tallest bar just fits. 1 cm = 5 would need 100 cm; 1 cm = 500 squashes everything into 1 cm.

q.t: Favourite sport: Cricket 45, Football 30, Hockey 15, Tennis 10. Find the mean number of students per sport.
Two bars are 3 cm and 4.5 cm tall and the scale is 1 cm = 20. Find the difference between the values they show.
q.e: The bars differ by 1.5 cm, and 1.5 × 20 = 30.

q.t: A double bar graph shows a student’s marks: Term 1 = 60, Term 2 = 75. Find the percentage improvement.
q.e: Increase = 15, measured on the starting value 60: 15/60 = 25%.

q.t: Rainfall (mm): June 120, July 200, August 180, September 100. Find the mean monthly rainfall (in mm).
Rainfall (mm): June 120, July 200, August 180, September 100. What percent of the total fell in July?
Rainfall (mm): July 200, September 100. By what percent is July’s rainfall more than September’s?
q.e: July is 100 mm more, compared with September’s 100: 100/100 = 100% more (double).

q.t: Rainfall (mm): June 120, August 180. Find the ratio of June to August.
The scale is 1 cm = 40 mm of rain. How tall is the bar for 180 mm (in cm)?
Double bar graph (boys, girls): Class A (20, 15), Class B (18, 22), Class C (25, 20). How many girls are there in all?
Double bar graph (boys, girls): Class A (20, 15), Class B (18, 22), Class C (25, 20). In which class is the girls’ bar taller than the boys’?
q.e: Only in B are there more girls (22) than boys (18).

q.t: Double bar graph (boys, girls): Class A (20, 15), Class B (18, 22), Class C (25, 20). How many students are there altogether?
Double bar graph (boys, girls): Class A (20, 15), Class B (18, 22), Class C (25, 20). What percent of all the students are boys?
Double bar graph (boys, girls): Class A (20, 15), Class B (18, 22), Class C (25, 20). How many more boys than girls are there in all?
Production (tonnes): 2019: 400, 2020: 500, 2021: 450, 2022: 600, 2023: 750. Find the percentage increase from 2022 to 2023.
q.e: Increase = 150 on a starting value of 600: 150/600 = 25%.

q.t: Production (tonnes): 2019: 400, 2020: 500, 2021: 450, 2022: 600, 2023: 750. Which year had the greatest PERCENTAGE increase over the year before?
q.e: 2020: 100/400 = 25%. 2021: a fall. 2022: 150/450 = 33 1/3%. 2023: 150/600 = 25%. The same rise of 150 is a bigger share of the smaller starting value.

q.t: Production (tonnes): 2019: 400, 2020: 500, 2021: 450, 2022: 600, 2023: 750. Find the mean yearly production (in tonnes).
Production (tonnes): 2019: 400, 2020: 500, 2021: 450, 2022: 600, 2023: 750. In how many years was production above the mean?
q.e: The mean is 540. Only 600 (2022) and 750 (2023) are above it.

q.t: Production (tonnes): 2019: 400, 2023: 750. Find the ratio of 2019 to 2023.
The scale is 1 cm = 50 tonnes. By how many centimetres do the bars for 500 tonnes and 750 tonnes differ?
Production in 2023 was 750 tonnes and in 2024 it is 20% more. With a scale of 1 cm = 50 tonnes, how tall is the 2024 bar (in cm)?
Production (tonnes): 400, 500, 450, 600, 750. Find the median (in tonnes).
q.e: In order: 400, 450, 500, 600, 750. The middle value is 500.

q.t: Production fell from 500 tonnes in 2020 to 450 tonnes in 2021. Find the percentage decrease.
q.e: Fall = 50 on a starting value of 500: 10%.

q.t: Production (tonnes): 2019: 400, 2020: 500, 2021: 450, 2022: 600, 2023: 750. What fraction of the five-year total was produced in 2021?
